caption:
In the highlands of Costa Rica, the straightest line between two valleys is always a ridge. Here, mountain biking is less about maintaining a perfect cadence and more about negotiating with gravity on grass, clay, and stone. When the slope climbs past twenty percent, the bike becomes something you carry as much as something you ride. But once you reach the spine of the mountain, with the forest falling away on both sides, the effort disappears into the silence of the clouds. Send this to the one who would climb this ridge with you.
